title: How to Choose Your First Three Processes
summary: Learn which three processes to structure first so each one makes the next easier to build.
body_markdown:
To **choose your first three processes** , pick them as a set rather than one at a time. Three processes that share data compound; three unrelated ones are three separate projects.


## Why the set matters more than each one


Shared records are what make the second and third faster.


- An isolated process gains nothing from what exists
- Client and supplier records built once serve everything after
- Adjacent processes create a connected view nobody had before
- Momentum depends on each build being easier than the last


## A combination that works


Process Why it fits the set


**First: the painful one** Visible relief earns permission for more


**Second: shares its records** Faster to build, immediately more useful


**Third: closes a loop** Connects the first two into a picture


## How to sequence it in Jestor


1. Build the most painful process in **Jestor** and get it genuinely running.
2. Capture its baseline **SLA** data before anything changes.
3. Choose a second that shares its client, supplier, or product records.
4. Choose a third that connects the first two — reporting, or a handoff between them.
5. Reuse structures by duplicating rather than rebuilding.


## Why choose Jestor for compounding builds?


Because processes share the same relational tables in **Jestor** , a client record built for the first process serves every process added afterwards without duplication.


Duplication copies structure and automations without records, so the second and third builds start from decisions already made rather than from a blank page.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Should I pick processes one at a time?


Pick them as a set that shares data. See[jestor.com](https://jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


### Which comes first?


The most painful and most visible.


### Does the second start from scratch?


No, duplication carries structure and automations.
